messages:
mario: Heads up — after the release merge (PR #1247) our nightly perf job shows a clear regression. p95 token generation for small prompts jumped ~18% compared to yesterday. log excerpt below:

mario: \`p95: 48ms -> 57ms (+18.8%)\`

ashley: Ugh. Is this on canary or master?

mario: Canary. Deploy history points to merge of PR #1247 (runtime:kernel-selection refactor). Canary config: g4dn, batch_size=8, seq=128.

jess: Can someone run a quick local repro? If it's kernel-selection related we might see different kernels chosen at short seq lengths.

sam: I'll kick off git bisect on a local minimal benchmark. Using this script: 

sam: ```bash
# perf-smoke.sh
python benchmarks/throughput_smoke.py --model small --batch 8 --seq 128 --runs 100
```

ci-bot: nightly/perf-check failed (regression detected, job id: 2026-03-10_03). See: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/2026-03-10_03

mario: CI flamegraphs show more time in attention kernel_selector path post-PR. KV cache hit rate also slightly lower in traces (misses up ~2%).

ashley: 2% miss sounds small, but combined with suboptimal kernel choice could blow p95. Any flamegraph snippets?

jess: Pasting small profiler output from local run before/after PR (abridged):

jess: ```
# before PR
attention::fused_kernel        42.3%
kv_cache::lookup              5.1%
other                         52.6%

# after PR
attention::generic_kernel      57.9%
kv_cache::lookup              7.4%
other                         34.7%
```

mario: That matches: fallback to generic kernel + extra cache overhead.

sam: git bisect progress: starting between v1.92 (good) and HEAD (bad). Running bisect with perf-smoke script.

sam: ```bash
git bisect start v1.92 HEAD
git bisect run ./scripts/perf-smoke.sh
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused due to perf regression alert. Manual approval required to resume.

ci-bot: Note — perf-check compares p95 over 3 runs, threshold 5% by default. This hit 18%.

ashley: If you get a suspect commit please paste the commit hash + short diff. Also include whether reverting it locally recovers perf.

sam: First bisect pass pinned commit 7f3c9a2 as first bad. It's the kernel selector refactor (changes in heuristics + fallback ordering).

mario: 7f3c9a2? That's the PR merge. Sam, can you try reverting that commit and rerun the smoke?

sam: Reverted locally and re-ran: p95 back to ~49ms. Quick logs: 

sam: \`p95: 57ms -> 49ms (regression removed)\`

jess: Good repro. Looks like the refactor changed tie-breaking logic in kernel_picker to prefer generic kernels for short sequences when quantized path exists.

ashley: Is the change safe? Maybe the refactor introduced a cost estimation bug. We need to fix commit rather than revert if possible — but hold rollout until patched.

mario: Can someone run a targeted micro-benchmark that toggles the kernel decision code path to confirm? I can add instrumentation if needed.

jess: I added a quick flag toggle in runtime: \`--force-old-kernel-order\` and ran bench: forcing old order recovers perf. Pasted command: 

jess: ```bash
./bin/runtime --bench seq=128 batch=8 --force-old-kernel-order
```

jess: Result: p95 ~49ms. Without flag: p95 ~57ms.

ashley: That isolates it. Sam — can you open a revert+fix PR: revert the refactor commit and reapply changes with correct cost model? Label as rollback-candidate and tag me.

sam: On it. I'll include perf regression test in CI that runs the smoke bench on merge.

ci-bot: FYI — adding perf smoke to PR checks will increase CI time by ~6m. Suggest running on merges to main only.

deploy-bot: Canary remains paused. Please request manual resume when fix merged and perf checks green.

mario: Thanks team. Next steps: sam opens PR, jess reviews kernel cost model, ashley signs off on perf test. After merge we rerun nightly and then unpause canary.

sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1283 (revert+fix). Includes microbench results and reasoning in the PR description.

jess: Reviewing now. Small nit on cost formula — I'll push suggestion.

mario: Appreciate the quick hunt. We should add a short postmortem note in the PR summarizing KV cache delta + kernel fallback impact for future. :thumbsup:

ashley: Agreed. Also add a link to this thread in the PR body.

ci-bot: PR 1283 triggered: perf-smoke passed on review runner (3 runs) — p95 within baseline.

deploy-bot: Manual resume requested. Waiting for security window slot.

mario: I'll coordinate resume after security approves.

sam: Closing bisect — culprit confirmed as 7f3c9a2. Repro, revert+fix PR opened.

jess: Nice triage.

mario: Thanks everyone.
